disclosure: Run 8 reuses the same SWE-bench dev validation case after seven disclosed runs. Run 7 passed its frozen target, 145-test regression, classification, path, invariant, and verifier gates, but a later source-level compatibility audit found duplicate-keyword and name-versus-type residual risks. Run 8 adds that audit as a mandatory factory probe. It remains policy-guided tuning, not independent generalization, a test-set score, an aggregate benchmark, a production claim, or a ranking claim.
priorRunFeedback: Run 1 fabricated unified-diff metadata; use exact-source replacement contracts instead.
Run 2 changed comments only and left target, regression, and token-classification checks failing.
Run 3 changed BaseSegment.is_whitespace globally; target and regression passed but ordinary code tokens became whitespace.
Run 4 preserved BaseSegment and localized ordinary whitespace behavior, but newline classification still failed.
Run 5 set is_whitespace on ANSI lexer entries; simple classification passed, but multiline-comment subdivision still failed.
Run 6 received factory-level feedback but repeated the same rejected ANSI lexer-entry changes twice.
Run 7 used the machine-allowed raw.py path and passed its pre-registered target, 145-test regression, token classification, protected invariant, and verifier gates.
A post-run factory probe found Run 7's name-based derivation fails aliases whose type is whitespace or newline and raises TypeError when callers explicitly pass is_whitespace.
Derive the default from kwargs type, preserve an explicitly supplied is_whitespace value, and avoid passing the same keyword twice into dict construction.
